predecessors.name: Duchy of Burgundy
predecessors.text: 'Upon the death of Mary of Burgundy in 1482, her substantial possessions including the Burgundian Netherlands passed to her son' (infobox 'Inherited by House of Habsburg: 1482')

successors.name: Dutch Republic
successors.text: the Seven United Provinces that 'seceded from the rest of this territory' in 1581

successors.name: French First Republic
successors.text: the Austrian Netherlands annexed after Fleurus (26 June 1794) and Sprimont (18 September 1794); 'On 1 October 1795 the departments were activated and the definitive annexation started'

rulers.name: Isabella Clara Eugenia and Archduke Albert VII

ledger.x: 1482: the Burgundian Netherlands pass to the Habsburgs.
23 May 1493: the Treaty of Senlis returns Artois.
1524: Friesland comes to Charles V.
1528: Utrecht and Overijssel.
1536: Groningen.
1543: Charles V re-acquires Guelders and the Seventeen Provinces are complete.
1549: the Pragmatic Sanction makes the Seventeen Provinces one entity: 'the Emperor's Pragmatic Sanction of 1549, which established the Seventeen Provinces as an entity'.
1556: the Netherlands pass to Philip II of Spain.
April 1572: Holland and Zeeland rise.
23 January 1579: Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht and Groningen sign the Union of Utrecht.
23 January 1579: Holland and Zeeland sign the Union of Utrecht; the contest of 1572 ends as the loss below and the lands are the Union's.
Summer 1579: Ghent, Antwerp, Ypres, Breda, Brussels, Amersfoort, Friesland and Guelders join the Union.
February 1580: Bruges and Lier join.
3 March 1580: Rennenberg returns Groningen to the king.
April 1580: Overijssel and Drenthe sign on.
1581: the Seven United Provinces secede.
1585: Parma retakes Flanders and Brabant.
1588 (bridging): the east is Spanish.
1590: the Dutch take Breda.
1591: the Dutch take Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl and Nijmegen: 'Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl, and Nijmegen in 1591'.
1592: the Dutch take Steenwijk and Coevorden: 'Steenwijk and Coevorden in 1592'.
1594: the Dutch take Groningen: 'Groningen in 1594'; the George van Lalaing page: the city 'remained the scene of military action until 1594'.
1597: the Dutch take Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum and Oldenzaal: 'and Grol, Enschede, Ootmarsum, and Oldenzaal in 1597'.
1606 (confidence 2): Spinola's campaign brings back Groenlo and Oldenzaal.
1625: Spain retakes Breda.
1626: the Dutch conquer Oldenzaal: 'the eastern border forts of Oldenzaal (1626) and Groenlo (1627)'.
1627: the Dutch conquer Groenlo: 'Oldenzaal (1626) and Groenlo (1627)'.
1629: the Dutch take 's-Hertogenbosch.
1632: the Dutch take the Meuse towns.
May 1635: France invades the Spanish Netherlands.
1637: the Dutch retake Breda.
1637: the Cardinal-Infante retakes Venlo and Roermond.
1645: Hulst falls to the Dutch.
24 June 1658: Dunkirk is lost after the Battle of the Dunes.
7 November 1659: the Treaty of the Pyrenees gives France Artois.
7 November 1659: Montmédy and other parts of Luxembourg go to France ('Montmédy and other parts of Luxembourg').
November 1659: the Franco-Spanish War ends; France keeps 'Artois and Hainaut along its border with the Spanish Netherlands'.
24 May 1667: France invades in the War of Devolution.
2 May 1668: Aix-la-Chapelle.
2 May 1668: the War of Devolution ends: 'signed by Spain and France on 2 May'.
1677: the French offensive on the Spanish Netherlands.
1677: Valenciennes, Cambrai, Saint-Omer, Cassel and Maubeuge fall.
1678 (bridging): Courtrai is Spanish again.
Early March 1678: the French take Ghent and Ypres: 'captured Ypres and Ghent in early March'.
Early March 1678: Ypres is lost to France and kept at Nijmegen.
17 September 1678: France returns Ghent.
17 September 1678: Spain recovers Charleroi and Ath.
17 September 1678: the Treaty of Nijmegen.
November 1683: the War of the Reunions.
November 1683: Courtrai and Diksmuide surrender.
3 June 1684: Luxembourg falls.
15 August 1684: the Truce of Ratisbon: 'guaranteeing 20 years of peace between France and the Empire'; France retained 'Strasbourg and Luxembourg'.
8 April 1691: Mons falls.
June 1692: Namur falls.
1694: the Allies capture Diksmuide.
5 September 1695: Namur is retaken.
1697: Ryswick restores Luxembourg, Mons and Courtrai.
1706: an Anglo-Dutch condominium.
1713 (bridging): Ypres, Tournai, Oudenaarde and Veurne are Austrian Netherlands.
1713: Venlo goes to the Dutch Republic.
7 March 1714: the condominium ends at Rastatt: 'the Southern Netherlands returned to the Austrian Habsburg monarchy'.
7 March 1714: the Spanish Netherlands become the Austrian Netherlands.
1715: Dutch Barrier garrisons.
1744: France occupies the Austrian Netherlands.
1748: Aix-la-Chapelle returns the land.
1781 (bridging): the Barrier ends.
27 October 1789: the Brabant Revolution.
January 1790: the United Belgian States are established, 'established in January 1790' and without foreign recognition.
December 1790: Austria crushes the revolution: 'the revolution was defeated by December' (after the Battle of Falmagne, 22 September 1790).
December 1790: the Austrian reconquest ends the Belgian revolt.
26 June 1794: Fleurus opens the Low Countries to France.
1 October 1795: France annexes.
1 October 1795: the Austrian Netherlands become French departments (lead: 'Revolutionary France annexed the territory after the Battle of Sprimont in 1794 and the Peace of Basel in 1795').

wars.name: Eighty Years' War (Southern Netherlands)
wars.outcome: Parma retakes Flanders and Brabant (Antwerp 1585); the Republic wins Breda (1590, lost 1625, regained 1637), 's-Hertogenbosch (1629), the Meuse towns (1632) and Hulst (1645); Münster (30 January 1648) leaves the south 'under Spanish Habsburg sovereignty'.

wars.name: Franco-Spanish War (1635-1659)
wars.outcome: Treaty of the Pyrenees, 7 November 1659: France gains most of Artois and Montmédy; the English receive Dunkirk.

wars.name: War of Devolution
wars.outcome: Aix-la-Chapelle (2 May 1668): France keeps Lille, Douai, Armentières, Bergues, Courtrai, Oudenaarde, Tournai, Veurne and Charleroi; Franche-Comté and Cambrai, Aire, Saint-Omer are returned.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War
wars.outcome: Nijmegen (17 September 1678): France keeps Ypres, Maubeuge, Valenciennes, Cambrai, Saint-Omer, Cassel and the Franche-Comté; returns Charleroi and Ghent.

wars.name: War of the Reunions
wars.outcome: Truce of Ratisbon (15 August 1684): France keeps Luxembourg; Ryswick (1697) restores the reunions.

wars.name: Nine Years' War (Spanish Netherlands front)
wars.outcome: France takes Mons (8 April 1691) and Namur (June 1692); William III retakes Namur on 5 September 1695; the Allies take Diksmuide in the 1694 campaign; the Peace of Ryswick (1697) has France evacuate 'Luxembourg, Mons and Kortrijk in the Spanish Netherlands'.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: An Anglo-Dutch condominium from 1706; Utrecht and Rastatt (7 March 1714) pass the Southern Netherlands to Austria.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession (Austrian Netherlands)
wars.outcome: France occupies the land; Aix-la-Chapelle returns it to Maria Theresa in 1748.

wars.name: Brabant Revolution
wars.outcome: The rebels win at Turnhout (27 October 1789) and form the United Belgian States (January 1790); Austria reconquers by December 1790.

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars (Austrian Netherlands)
wars.outcome: Fleurus (26 June 1794) and Sprimont (18 September 1794) end Austrian rule; annexation on 1 October 1795.

certainty.note: The pages give provinces and towns, not boundaries; the provincial frontiers are those of the Seventeen Provinces.
The frontier with the Union and the Republic moves with sieges; Münster (1648) fixes the northern one.
Treaty lines of 1659, 1668, 1678, 1697 and 1714 fix the French and Dutch frontiers; the Luxembourg and Barrier enclaves are approximate.
